# Storytelling

A stakeholder demo is a short product video: the running app, a user doing real things with it, and a
narrator explaining what is happening and how to use it. Aim for one to three minutes. Show the app, not
slides.

Every demo has the narrator, whatever kind of app it is. The browser, terminal and HTTP adapters are
only ways of using the app, chosen per scene from what the app needs. When the story needs an interaction
they cannot perform, a run-local helper written for this app performs it
([run-local-helpers.md](run-local-helpers.md)); its media appears only where the story needs it, labelled
with what it is. Never invent extra voices or roles an app does not have.

## One journey, all user-visible features

Write one journey a real user would follow, from opening the app to getting what they came for. Cover
every user-visible feature you can show in that journey; list each one in the plan's `features` as shown
(with its scenes) or left out (with a reason the human can read). If the app has more than one fits in a
few minutes, ask the human which matter most rather than dropping them silently.

## Audiences

- **Business**: the person, their goal, what changes for them. Plain words, no internals, no unmeasured
  numbers.
- **Engineering**: the same scenes, with the entry point, request or command and what was checked. Name
  files and interfaces the evidence covers.

Every scene needs narration for every declared audience, and each narration line cites the claims it
makes. QA checks that an audience's narration is grounded in its own scene's actions.

## Scene template

For each scene in the storyboard:

- `id`, `title`, `adapter`: `browser` (a recorded page), `process` (a terminal command) or `http` (one
  request);
- `capabilities` from the catalog and `dataProvenance` ids;
- `actions`: `run` with a command ref, `request` with a request ref, or the page ops `goto`, `click`,
  `fill`, `press` and `wait` (see [platform-support.md](platform-support.md)), and in browser scenes
  `helper` with the `ref` of a declared interaction and its input in `value` (below);
- `expect` checks for those actions (`exitCode`, `stdoutIncludes`, `stderrIncludes`, `status`,
  `bodyIncludes`, `pageIncludes`, `pageExcludes`, `pageIncludesNew`);
- `narration` per audience with `claims` and `caption` provenance;
- optional `diagram` naming catalog edges and a caption, only when the plan sets
  `allowArchitectureCards`.

## Scenes with a run-local helper

When the interaction is the demo (for example a simulated user talking to an app that listens), open the
app in the recorded browser, use page ops to get to the right place, then a `helper` action. Give it a
`pageIncludesNew` expectation: text the app shows only once this interaction has happened. That check is
a safeguard against stale text, not proof that the reply is the current one; the helper must tie the
reply to its own action, or report `unknown`.

Write any simulated user's input like a real first-time user: short, natural and about what the app
offers. Never script the app's replies. A helper's generated media is captioned as generated by the
helper, never as the app.

## Narration and captions

Narration is drafted by you (`agent-drafted`) or supplied by a human (`human-supplied`). Captions derive
from it. Explain what the viewer sees and how a user would do it themselves. `produce` synthesizes the
narration offline and times captions from the real audio:

- browser, process and HTTP scenes: narration plays over the clip, which holds its last frame while
  narration finishes;
- scenes with helper media: narration plays first over a still of the scene's first frame, then the
  recorded clip plays with the helper's media and without narration, so they never overlap. Keep that
  narration to a short introduction of what is about to happen.

## Diagrams

Off by default. Only with `allowArchitectureCards: true` may a scene carry a diagram, and it may only
show catalog edges. Say in its caption whether the path is exercised in this run or is a code path only
(`inferred`).

## Data, privacy and rights

- Prefer synthetic data. Declare each data source in `dataProvenance` with its kind.
- Human-supplied data needs `rightsConfirmed: true`.
- If confidentiality says `synthetic-only`, every scene's data must be synthetic.
- Never show secrets, personal data or customer content. Discovery never reads them; do not paste them in.
